original_question: Assume X subseteq B subseteq R, B is Borel, and X satisfies Ufin(O,Gamma). Must there exist a sigma-compact set F with X subset F subset B? Also, if the Borel assumption on B is strengthened to B being F_{sigma delta}, is the conclusion true?
target_in_paper: arXiv:math/0609601, Section 2, Problem 2.3. The nearby official context is the immediately preceding characterization of Ufin(O,Γ) by interpolation inside Gδ supersets, and the cited Banakh–Zdomskyy source recasts the same issue as asking whether Hurewicz spaces have stronger separation properties, especially the F_{σδ}/G_{δ}F_{σ} one.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost verbatim: it has the right setting X⊆B⊆ℝ, the right hypothesis Ufin(O,Γ) (the Hurewicz property), the right interpolation conclusion via a σ-compact set F, and the right second clause asking specifically about the F_{σδ} case.
missing_details: Spell out Ufin(O,Γ): for every sequence (𝒰_n)n∈ω of open covers of X, there are finite subfamilies 𝒱_n⊆𝒰_n such that {⋃𝒱_n : n∈ω} is a γ-cover of X, i.e. each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many ⋃𝒱_n.
Say explicitly that this is a problem about sets of reals, i.e. subspaces of ℝ with the usual topology.
Mention the paper’s nearby context: Problem 2.3 is posed as an extension of the preceding fact that X satisfies Ufin(O,Γ) iff for every Gδ set G⊆ℝ with X⊆G there is a σ-compact F with X⊂F⊂G.
Use the paper-faithful two-part formulation with the intermediate set written as X⊂F⊂B, matching the official wording.

If aligning with the cited source paper, note that the second clause is the question whether Hurewicz spaces have the stronger F_{σδ}-separation property; Banakh–Zdomskyy formulate a closely related class as G_{δ}F_{σ}, the class of spaces that are unions of a Polish subspace and a σ-compact subspace.

Do not alter the hypothesis to the stronger property Sfin(B,Γ): the cited source proves Borel interpolation under that stronger assumption, but Problem 2.3 keeps the weaker Hurewicz hypothesis Ufin(O,Γ).
refined_question: Let X⊆ℝ be a set of reals with the Hurewicz property Ufin(O,Γ); that is, for every sequence (𝒰_n)n∈ω of open covers of X there exist finite subfamilies 𝒱_n⊆𝒰_n such that {⋃𝒱_n:n∈ω} is a γ-cover of X. Suppose X⊆B⊆ℝ and B is Borel. Must there exist a σ-compact set F with X⊂F⊂B? In particular, is this always true when B is an F_{σδ} subset of ℝ?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since the paper recalls that X satisfies Ufin(O,Γ) iff every Gδ superset G of X contains a σ-compact F with X⊂F⊂G, does this interpolation property extend from Gδ supersets to Borel supersets, and at least to F_{σδ} supersets?
justification: The draft is essentially the exact content of Problem 2.3 in the survey arXiv:math/0609601. The sentence immediately before Problem 2.3 gives the known Gδ interpolation characterization of Ufin(O,Γ), so the paper’s intent is specifically to ask whether that characterization extends to larger descriptive classes, first Borel and then F_{σδ}. The cited Banakh–Zdomskyy paper supplies the hidden context: all spaces are metrizable and separable; Hurewicz spaces are exactly those with the Gδ-separation property; and the paper studies stronger separation properties for larger classes. In particular, Banakh–Zdomskyy show that the stronger F_{σδ}/G_{δ}F_{σ} direction can consistently fail, while also proving that the Borel interpolation conclusion does hold under the strictly stronger hypothesis Sfin(B,Γ). So the sharp, paper-faithful reformulation is the two-part interpolation question above, with Ufin(O,Γ) defined explicitly and no hypothesis changes.
